news.title: Fight over climate science intensifies at COP31
news.summary: The EU, AOSIS and LDCs back IPCC reports in 2028, while Saudi Arabia, China and India push to delay to 2029; IPCC chair Skea warns of reputational risks from the impasse.

news.title: COP31 talks face early friction over future of fossil fuels
news.summary: As week one closes, oil and coal interests resist firm targets; Turkey centres a deal on electrification while the EU says it must be clean, and Australia aims for a consensus draft early next week.

news.title: COP31 deal wish list includes fossil fuel transition
news.summary: The presidencies' Summary of Reflections includes the COP28 fossil-fuel transition, limiting overshoot, tripling adaptation finance and the IPCC's role; a first draft may come Monday, and the EU sees no will for new funding pledges.

news.title: Analysis: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
news.summary: Island leaders from Solomon Islands and the Marshall Islands press for faster finance as the $300bn and $1.3tn goals lag; Bowen calls for finance that is 'faster, simpler and fairer'.

news.title: COP31: Carbon removal and CCUS included in COP31 cover decision talks
news.summary: The presidency's informal summary of Party views lists CCUS and CDR deployment, with safeguards, alongside overshoot limits, 35x35 electrification and methane action; it is not a consensus text.

news.title: COP31 Bulletin Day 5: Cover decision wishlist issued as China bows out of COP33
news.summary: The presidencies' summary of reflections lists possible cover decision elements; the EU backs addressing overshoot and methane, while a trade-measures call is read as aimed at the EU carbon border levy.

news.title: EU recommits to 2050 climate-neutral target at COP31
news.summary: At an EU press conference, the Commission's Diana Acconcia and Ireland's Philip Nugent set out priorities: overshoot, delivery and adaptation.

news.title: Ireland signs pact to grow carbon credits market for investors at Cop31
news.summary: Ireland, which leads the EU delegation at COP31, has signed up to a pact intended to expand the market for carbon credits.

news.title: Pacific leaves empty handed from COP31 "pledging event" for new fund
news.summary: Developed countries only repeated earlier pledges to the Pacific Resilience Facility, including the Netherlands and Ireland, leaving it about $300m short of its 2026 target of $500m.

news.title: COP31 – Dan Jørgensen says EU backs Brazilian 'roadmap' for transition away from fossil fuels
news.summary: Jørgensen said the EU supports the fossil fuel transition roadmap presented by Brazil's COP30 Presidency, while von der Leyen's speech backed the 35x35 electrification pledge without explicitly mentioning fossil fuels, drawing criticism from CAN Europe.

news.title: Push for ocean roadmap that informs next global stocktake grows at COP31
news.summary: Calls are growing at COP31 for an ocean roadmap designed to inform the next global stocktake.

news.title: Chris Bowen seeks pragmatic consensus heading into final COP31 talks
news.summary: Bowen says he will steer consensus to the most ambitious outcome possible, calls the fossil-fuel transition 'challenging' and defends the 35x35 electrification goal not requiring 100% renewables.

news.title: World leaders clash over climate change talks at COP31
news.summary: Two days of speeches leave negotiators a tough task: European leaders back expanded electrification, islands demand deep cuts and developing countries seek finance.

news.title: World leaders set out clashing priorities as COP31 turns to negotiations
news.summary: European leaders rally behind global electrification, small islands plead for deep cuts, developing countries seek finance and Venezuela defends oil expansion as talks shift to negotiators.

news.title: COP31's electrification pledge wins support, with caveats on clean power and finance
news.summary: At least 14 countries back the voluntary 35x35 pledge, including Germany, Finland and Norway; the EU is expected to join, while island states warn against distraction from fossil-fuel transition.

news.title: Burnham commits to 2050 net zero target and working with others to reach theirs
news.summary: In a five-minute speech, Burnham backs 2050 net zero and Türkiye's electrification goal; the UK will publish a clean electrification road map ahead of a UK-EU summit in Brussels.

news.title: UK names a climate security envoy as island leaders warn of a 'life-or-death' crisis
news.summary: Leaders' Summit day two: Burnham appoints a climate security representative; Pacific and island leaders press for loss-and-damage finance as Climate Action Tracker projects 2.6°C.

news.title: COP31 Bulletin Day 4: Burnham speaks with UK climate policy under fire
news.summary: Day-two Leaders' Summit preview: the UK prime minister is among 25 leaders due to speak, with Lula, Greta Thunberg and Gavin Newsom also expected to draw attention.

news.title: Major leaders missing as COP31 runs in Turkey
news.summary: Macron, Merz and Meloni stay away from the high-level segment; NGOs warn von der Leyen may be 'lonely on the stage' as Hoekstra plays down expectations.

news.title: Analysis: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as countries meet at COP31
news.summary: Public climate-finance pledges drop about 70% in 2026; the Commission averages $4.5bn a year to 2027, and Hoekstra says new money is 'dead in the water'.

news.title: Albanese: COP31 must deliver practical results at Antalya summit
news.summary: Australia's PM, whose country holds the negotiations presidency, urges practical outcomes and highlights the Pacific Resilience Facility.

news.title: 'Make or bake time': Guterres urges climate justice pact as leaders gather at COP31
news.summary: Guterres sets out a climate justice compact, urges windfall taxes on fossil-fuel firms and a near-zero methane standard; Erdoğan and Lula speak on implementation and roadmaps.

news.title: World leaders speak at COP31 climate conference
news.summary: Key lines from Guterres, Erdogan, Lula, Han Zheng, Albanese, von der Leyen, Slovenia's Pirc Musar and others at the Antalya Leaders' Summit.

news.title: Daily Briefing: World leaders at COP31
news.summary: Round-up of leaders' summit coverage, wavering support for the 35-by-35 electrification pledge and backing for Brazil's fossil-transition roadmap.

news.title: COP31, von der Leyen: "L'Ue punta all'obiettivo del 46% di elettricità nei consumi entro il 2040"
news.summary: Von der Leyen backs the 35-by-35 electrification pledge, cites the EU's 46%-by-2040 electrification goal, over €32bn in climate finance last year and a 90% emissions cut target for 2040 (in Italian).

news.title: War, conflict must not distract from climate action, leaders warn COP31
news.summary: Lula, Erdogan and Guterres warn that wars and geopolitical rivalry are crowding out climate action, as talks centre on Türkiye's electrification proposal and stalled fossil-fuel transition efforts.

news.title: COP31 Bulletin Day 3: With the people stuck outside, world leaders jet in
news.summary: Road closures for around 40 leaders, including von der Leyen, Lula and Erdoğan, disrupt access to the venue; Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt, the Netherlands and Sweden drop off the speakers' list.

news.title: UN chief urges world leaders to tackle fossil fuels at COP31
news.summary: At his final COP, Guterres says the climate crisis is outrunning the world, calls for ending fossil-fuel addiction and taxing oil windfall profits; von der Leyen attends as Macron, Merz and Meloni stay away.

news.title: COP31 electric power target sparks row over cutting fossil fuel use
news.summary: Türkiye's 35-by-35 electrification goal meets resistance as draft wording does not require clean power; Australia's rooftop-solar pledge adds five countries.

news.title: Christodoulides, von der Leyen discuss Cyprus problem in Antalya
news.summary: Cyprus's president met the Commission President on the COP31 sidelines to discuss the Cyprus problem and EU relations, and raised his reception by Erdogan earlier in the day.

news.title: Erdogan holds six meetings and signs Saudi power deal as COP31 turns to energy
news.summary: Erdogan met six leaders including Guterres and witnessed a Türkiye–Saudi electricity MoU on solar, wind and HVDC transmission; COP31 counts over 68,500 registered participants.

news.title: 'More than just a photo opportunity': Why are key EU leaders skipping the COP31 Leaders' Summit?
news.summary: Merz, Macron, Meloni and Sánchez miss the summit while von der Leyen represents the EU; the piece also covers the EU climate progress report, with Hoekstra to seek corrective plans from nine member states.

news.title: World leaders take stage at COP31 but big names missing
news.summary: AFP notes several major European leaders are skipping Antalya while von der Leyen attends; the EU insists Türkiye's electrification push must be clean. CAN Europe warned von der Leyen "will be lonely on the stage".

news.title: World leaders gather at COP31 as fossil fuel talks stall
news.summary: Reuters reports the fossil-fuel question remains unresolved as leaders arrive, with Türkiye's 35% electrification goal carrying no clean-power requirement.

news.title: World leaders to address COP31 as Turkey pushes for new climate deal
news.summary: Reuters preview of the leaders' segment opening on day three, as host Türkiye presses for a new climate deal.

news.title: COP31: Energy transition takes centre stage as countries map path beyond fossil fuels
news.summary: Energy day: Brazil presents its voluntary fossil-transition roadmap; Guterres cites €100bn in extra EU fossil import costs.

news.title: Big fossil-fuel countries back Brazil-led transition roadmap
news.summary: Several major fossil-fuel producers support the COP30 Presidency's transition roadmap; Germany and the Netherlands want such roadmaps to feed into the 2028 global stocktake.

news.title: EU climate chief says expectations low for COP31, urges focus on clean electricity
news.summary: Hoekstra told reporters expectations were 'a reflection of reality', called recent COPs underwhelming, ruled out appetite for new finance pledges and pushed for electrification to be the core of the conclusions.

news.title: COP31 seeks faster action as energy security concerns grow
news.summary: Energy Day coverage: Kurum, Bowen and Stiell press conference on the 35% electricity-share target, and a joint declaration of support for Kurum from former COP presidents.

news.title: COP31 Bulletin Day 2: Energy Day off to slow start amid transport chaos
news.summary: Electrification pledge and its uncertain place in the cover decision, Guterres at Brazil's fossil-fuel roadmap launch, EU-co-hosted Electrification Forum, coal and solar initiatives, and warnings of severe disruption for Wednesday's leaders' segment.

voices.name: Samed Ağırbaş

voices.name: Lynda Tabuya

position.headline: A mitigation package, not a headline target

points.v: Accepts 1.5°C is likely to be exceeded; backs an overshoot-peak-decline pathway to return below 1.5°C by 2100.
Effective implementation of national plans and urgent submission of missing NDCs.
Deliver the first global stocktake: transition away from fossil fuels and an accelerated clean energy transition, with clean electrification central.
Space in the talks for mitigation and a steer for the second global stocktake. Reuters reports the EU wants the mitigation work programme extended to 2040.
Mitigation and adaptation treated as complementary; resilience a prerequisite for prosperity.
Separate Council conclusions on climate finance adopted 9 Oct.
Stresses that all EU member states take part in COP31, a reference to Cyprus's exclusion from preparatory talks.

watch: Whether France's call for a more transactional line with emerging economies shapes EU tactics on the floor.
How the EU uses coalitions outside consensus talks, which Hoekstra has favoured.
Cyprus: Türkiye's handling of a member state the EU insists must participate.
The EU's proposed design for a Just Transition Mechanism, discussed by member states in September.

announcements.text: COP31 opened after a slight delay caused by debate over adding finance items to the agenda; COP30 President André Corrêa do Lago declared the session open.
Greece attends COP31 led by Environment and Energy Minister Stavros Papastavrou; Cyprus's President was invited after pressure from Athens, Nicosia and EU institutions.
Climate Home understands African states agreed overnight to withdraw their request for extra agenda items on adaptation finance and trade; talks on Nepal's mountain item continued Monday.
Bowen tells the opening plenary the COP31 cover decision will bring 'no surprises': a short, practical text, not a lengthy political declaration.
Euronews: all 27 member states back the EU's COP31 position, but several put affordable, secure energy first; a Commission official calls fossil transition progress politically difficult.
Long entry queues at the Antalya Expo Centre on day one: one reporter waited over three hours, with delegates stuck in traffic or unable to board scarce shuttles.
Türkiye and WHO launch the voluntary Antalya Initiative for Resilient Health Systems on Health Day; no participants or funding announced yet.
The 44 Least Developed Countries call the 1.5°C overshoot 'a grave betrayal' and say COP31 cannot be another exercise in deferring difficult decisions.
Day two (Energy & Transport): about 370 sessions, 140 on the theme, incl. a Blue Zone ministerial on the Azerbaijan–Kazakhstan–Uzbekistan green energy link and a Ukraine energy panel.
Climate Home: big fossil-fuel countries back Brazil's transition roadmap; Germany and the Netherlands want the roadmaps to feed into the 2028 global stocktake.
Erdogan witnessed a Türkiye–Saudi Arabia electricity MoU covering about 2,000 MW of solar and a second phase of 3,000 MW of wind with HVDC links and storage.
Guterres says the EU alone has paid over €100 billion in extra fossil-fuel import costs since the Middle East escalation, as Brazil formally presents its fossil-transition roadmap.
AP: an adviser to African negotiators says African Group agenda proposals were backed by many developing countries but contested by the EU and Canada.
Business Standard: the opening agenda fight centred on the climate finance work programme, with G77/China seeking Article 9.1 talks and the EU and Umbrella Group resisting.
Trade measures such as the EU's CBAM were not added as a separate agenda item, but India and other developing countries say talks will continue through other channels.
Reuters: Türkiye will ask governments and others to sign a pledge on sustainable AI at COP31, alongside its push to electrify over a third of the economy by 2035.
Reuters: Türkiye will seek to put its 35%-by-2035 global electrification goal at the centre of COP31's final agreement, despite criticism it does not require clean power.
Portugal will push to tie Türkiye's electrification goal to low-carbon power; minister Maria da Graça Carvalho: 'not simply electrification, but clean electrification'.
Climate Diplomacy Brief: Brazil, Korea and Canada are said to back Türkiye's 35-by-35 electrification pledge, while the EU wavers over the missing word 'clean'.
The COP30 Presidency's fossil-fuel transition roadmap launch is scheduled for 13:00 Tuesday, with Brazil's President Lula expected to attend.
Badge queues persisted: some delegates reported waits of up to five hours, and return shuttles took two hours to cover 18 km.
Kurum, Bowen and Stiell held a joint press conference on Energy Day; Stiell cited a call by about 180 companies for $1.7 trillion in electrification investment.
Former COP presidents including Laurent Fabius, Alok Sharma, Michał Kurtyka and André Corrêa do Lago issued a joint declaration backing COP31 President Kurum.
At the COP30 Presidency's fossil-fuel roadmap launch, Guterres urged COP31 to 'move from discussing the transition to organising it', with progress shown by the 2028 stocktake.
Climate Home: fossil-fuel producers are expected to resist anchoring Brazil's roadmap or clean-power wording for the 35x35 electrification goal in the cover decision.
The EU co-hosts the first COP31 Electrification Forum on Tuesday with governments, institutions, businesses and financiers.
Presidency warns of 'severe disruptions' Wednesday: arrive by 7am, extra public transport 05:00–07:00, after which no public transport can leave the area.
42 world leaders are due to speak Wednesday from 14:00, including Commission President von der Leyen, Brazil's Lula and China's Vice President Han Zheng.
The Powering Past Coal Alliance launched Coal Transition Partnerships aiming to unlock over $23bn for ten coal-dependent countries by 2028.
Hoekstra says COP31 expectations are low, sees no political will for new finance pledges, and wants a clean electrification target at the heart of the outcome.
Australia's voluntary pledge to double rooftop-solar households to at least 300 million by 2030 gains Bangladesh, Kenya, Nigeria, Palau and Vanuatu.
Leaders' Summit: opening session 12:15 TRT, HLS opens 14:00; presidential round tables on electrification and green industry at 15:00 and 17:00. Resumed HLS 17–18 Nov.
Lula tells COP31 leaders climate change has 'disappeared' from global leaders' agendas; Erdogan says wars and crises raise the need for solidarity.
Von der Leyen tells the Leaders' Summit the EU backs Türkiye's 35-by-35 electrification pledge and aims to double electricity's share of EU energy use to 46% by 2040.
China's Vice President Han Zheng tells COP31 leaders developed countries should lead on emission cuts and honour their climate-finance commitments.
Slovenian President Nataša Pirc Musar warns leaders that a gradual energy transition must not become an excuse for endless delay.
AFP: von der Leyen attends the leaders' segment while Macron, Merz and Meloni skip it; Hoekstra calls the absences 'not completely atypical'.
COP31 has more than 68,500 registered participants plus about 24,500 workers on site, according to Türkiye Today.
Reuters: fossil-fuel talks stall as leaders arrive; Brazil's roadmap asks countries to plan energy systems by 2028 and cut fossil supply from 2031.
EU climate progress report: provisional net emissions fell 1.6% in 2025 to 39% below 1990; the Commission will ask nine member states for corrective action plans.
Euronews: Spain's Sánchez also skips the Leaders' Summit, and Denmark, Ireland and the Netherlands send no leader; von der Leyen speaks for the EU today.
Carbon Brief analysis: public climate-finance pledges to developing countries fall about 70% in 2026, with only five nations announcing new multi-year pledges.
Von der Leyen met Cypriot President Christodoulides on the COP31 sidelines to discuss the Cyprus problem and EU relations.
Roads around the COP31 venue were closed for the arrival of about 40 leaders; the UN later said organisers' advice to arrive by 7am was not necessary.
Guterres tells COP31 leaders the climate crisis is 'outrunning us', urging an end to fossil-fuel addiction and taxes on oil companies' windfall profits.
Australian PM Albanese tells the Leaders' Summit COP31 must deliver practical results, citing the Pacific-led Pacific Resilience Facility.
Guterres proposes a four-part 'climate justice compact' and asks UNEP to develop a global near-zero methane standard for oil and gas.
Leaders' Summit day two: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is among about 25 leaders due to address COP31 on Thursday, with UK climate policy under domestic criticism.
UK PM Andy Burnham tells COP31 climate is a national security issue, names Madeleine Alessandri special representative for climate security.
Climate Action Tracker says aggregate climate action has stalled for five years; current pledges, if met, point to 2.6°C warming by 2100.
Island leaders from Seychelles, Niue and the Marshall Islands warn of a 'life-or-death' crisis and urge a stronger loss-and-damage fund.
The COP31 Leaders' Summit concludes; WRI says electrification and the fossil-fuel transition took centre stage and calls for ocean action in the cover decision.
Final Leaders' Summit day focuses on resilient cities, building and transport electrification and a methane session; the COP31 Business Forum also opens.
Climate Home's day-4 bulletin reports emerging economies questioning whether COP31 needs a cover decision at all.
Palau President Surangel Whipps Jr says small island states must not be pushed into more debt to repair climate damage.
Climate Home reports a growing push at COP31 for an ocean roadmap that would feed into the next global stocktake.
Agence Europe: EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen says the EU backs the COP30 Presidency's roadmap for transitioning away from fossil fuels.
Burnham reaffirms UK 2050 net zero and endorses Türkiye's pledge to lift electricity's share of global energy demand from 21% to 35% by 2035.
Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif calls at COP31 for grant-based climate finance, describing adaptation funding as 'survival funds'.
At least 14 countries, including Germany, Finland and Norway, have endorsed the 35x35 electrification pledge; the EU is expected to join once member states approve.
Palau and Seychelles back the 35x35 pledge but warn electrification must not distract from moving away from fossil fuels; Saudi Arabia voices scepticism.
No new money at the COP31 pledging session for the Pacific Resilience Facility; the Netherlands, Ireland, UK and Canada only re-announced earlier pledges.
Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodríguez asserts a sovereign right to expand oil output, as fossil producers push back on calls to end the fossil fuel age.
With leaders' speeches over, COP31 negotiations president Chris Bowen tells Reuters he has 'many more hours of consultations' ahead to steer consensus.
Bowen says talks have a 'good spirit' but a 'long way to go', with negotiations ramping up next week; Australia seeks deals on electrification and finance.
Ireland signs a pact at COP31 aimed at growing the international carbon credits market for investors, the Irish Times reports.
COP31 presidencies publish a 'summary of reflections' on the cover decision, a non-consensus menu incl. overshoot, fossil transition roadmaps and 35x35; written views due Saturday.
Saudi Arabia and others question the UNEP overshoot report; the Arab group opposes any reference to the COP30 presidency's fossil fuel roadmaps in a decision.
Cover decision wishlist includes a call for a time-bound phase-out of unilateral climate trade measures, widely read as targeting the EU's carbon border levy.
China has ruled itself out of hosting COP33 in 2028, according to a Guardian report; no COP33 host decision is expected in Antalya.
AFP: a first draft of the COP31 cover decision could be published on Monday 16 November; Russia and the Arab Group say there is 'no mandate' for one.
Saudi Arabia, India and China want the next IPCC assessment delayed from 2028 to 2029, while the reflections list cites the IPCC's 'central role'.
The presidency's informal summary of 10–11 Nov consultations records calls to scale up CCUS and carbon removal, with safeguards, to reverse 1.5C overshoot.
Commission's Diana Acconcia says the EU will be climate-neutral by 2050, is on track for -55% by 2030, and backs addressing 1.5C overshoot in the outcome.
For the Irish Presidency, Philip Nugent calls talks 'so far so good' but says the business end is still ahead; adaptation is a core EU priority.
Reuters: vulnerable nations' urgent finance pleas meet a slow response; Bowen says climate finance must be 'faster, simpler and fairer'.
announcements.source: Reuters via Global Banking & Finance Review

announcements.text: EU delegation head Diana Acconcia says the EU backs the electrification goal but insists it must come from clean energy sources.
Reuters: fossil producers and big consumers resist firm new targets; Turkey's electrification proposal doesn't require renewables, Brazil pushes transition roadmaps.
EU's Diana Acconcia says the EU will fight for timely IPCC reports before the 2028 stocktake, accusing some parties of trying to undermine the science.
IPCC chair Jim Skea tells COP31 the panel faces operational challenges and reputational risks from the impasse over its next assessment timeline.
